title: Exclamaciones y suavizadores
summary: Reacting like a local: ¡qué va!, ¡anda!, ¡venga ya! and the softeners hombre/mujer, jolín

blocks.title: Reaccionar como un español
blocks.body: Spain reacts **out loud**. Half of sounding native is having the right little exclamation ready instead of a silent nod. **¡Qué va!** (no way / not at all), **¡Anda!** (huh! / wow), **¡Venga ya!** (oh come on / you're kidding). And the softeners — **hombre**, **mujer**, **jolín** — that take the edge off a sentence. Today you stop translating and start *reacting*.
blocks.callout: None of these translate cleanly. Learn the *feeling*, not the dictionary word.

blocks.title: *Hombre* y *mujer* no son 'man' y 'woman'
blocks.body: Dropped into a sentence, **hombre** and **mujer** aren't 'man/woman' — they're **softeners and emphasis**, and you say *hombre* to a woman too. *Hombre, no te preocupes* (come on, don't worry). *¿Vienes? — ¡Hombre, claro!* (Are you coming? — Well, of course!). **Jolín** is the soft, family-friendly cousin of a stronger word — mild frustration, like 'darn'.
blocks.callout: *¡Hombre!* on its own = pleased surprise: *¡Hombre, Rafa!* (Hey, Rafa!).

blocks.prompt: Tu amigo dice que ha corrido una maratón, pero sabes que odia correr. ¿Qué le dices?
blocks.explain: **¡Qué va!** expresses disbelief and denial — 'no way, I don't buy it'. *Jolín* is mild frustration and *¡qué pena!* is sympathy — neither fits teasing disbelief.

pairs.left: ¡Qué va! — no, not at all (you deny something)
pairs.right: ¡Venga ya! — oh come on! (you doubt or protest)
pairs.note: *¿Estás enfadado? — ¡Qué va!* (denial: no, not at all). *¿Te ha tocado la lotería? — ¡Venga ya!* (disbelief: get out of here).

blocks.prompt: Someone tells you gossip you find hard to believe. Type the two-word 'you're kidding / come on' reaction (with ¡!).
blocks.hint: Starts with the same word you use for 'come on'.
blocks.explain: *¡Venga ya!* — protest and disbelief in two words. Remember the opening ¡ and the closing !.

blocks.scene: Rafa drops some news on the terrace — react along with Lucía

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.target: ¿Te has enterado? Nacho se compra una casa en el pueblo.
lines.en: Have you heard? Nacho's buying a house in the village.

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.target: Que sí, tía. Y dice que Madrid es un agobio.
lines.en: Yeah, really. And he says Madrid is exhausting.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: Come on, he always says that!

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.target: ¡Qué va! Esta vez va en serio.
lines.en: Not at all! This time he means it.

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.target: Jolín, pues le voy a echar de menos en el bar.
lines.en: Darn, I'm going to miss him at the bar then.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: ¡Venga ya, si el pueblo está a una hora!
lines.en: Oh come on, the village is an hour away!

options: Que Nacho se compra una casa en el pueblo
Que Sofía se muda a Valencia

blocks.prompt: Piensa en tres cosas que te sorprenden de la vida en España. Reacciona a cada una con una exclamación distinta (*¡anda!, ¡qué fuerte!, ¡venga ya!…*). Escribe tres frases.
